text: I felt like it was a problem that was very solvable. And we ended up renting a stadium to just hire 60,000 drivers in a couple of weeks. So I think looking back, it was certainly a risk.
speaker: Crystal Widjaja
context: Crystal is introducing herself and her path to joining Gojek, the ride-hailing company that became Southeast Asia's largest super app. She's explaining how she took a major career risk by cold-emailing Gojek and moving to Indonesia to work for what was then a very early-stage startup. The quote illustrates the unconventional, massive-scale hiring approach they used to rapidly onboard drivers - literally renting a stadium to hire tens of thousands of people at once.
text_ko: 저는 그게 충분히 해결할 수 있는 문제라고 생각했어요. 결국 몇 주 만에 6만 명의 기사님을 모으기 위해 경기장을 통째로 빌렸어요. 돌이켜보면 분명히 큰 위험이었어요.
text_zh: 我当时觉得这个问题完全可以解决。后来我们直接租了个体育场，几周内就招了6万个司机。现在回头看，确实是挺冒险的。
text_es: Me pareció que era un problema que tenía solución. Y al final terminamos rentando un estadio para contratar 60,000 conductores en un par de semanas. Así que mirando hacia atrás, definitivamente fue un riesgo.
key_sentence: It was a problem very solvable, but I made a huge mistake.
original_text: I felt like it was a problem that was very solvable. And we ended up renting a stadium to just hire 60,000 drivers in a couple of weeks. So I think looking back, it was certainly a risk. When I got there it was in a house and I realized I've probably made a huge mistake, but we were growing very quickly already, even at that small scale of 4,000 orders per day.

vocabulary.definition: Capable of being resolved or dealt with successfully; having a solution.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a solvable problem refers to challenges that can be addressed through strategic planning, resource allocation, or innovative thinking.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often implies that the solution is within reach and may require effort but is not insurmountable.

vocabulary.definition: The possibility of loss, damage, or any other adverse outcome resulting from a decision or action.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and finance, risk assessment is crucial for making informed decisions, particularly in investments, project management, and strategic planning.
vocabulary.nuance: While risk often carries a negative connotation, it can also represent opportunities for growth and innovation when managed effectively.

text: I literally emailed someone after Googling HR at Gojek and said, 'I'm willing to move to Indonesia, take a bet on me.' And they actually did. So I got extremely lucky. Five years fly by insanely fast.
speaker: Crystal Widjaja
context: Lenny asks Crystal about her unusual career path from investment banking to becoming a key growth leader at Gojek. Crystal explains how she made the transition by cold-emailing startups in Southeast Asia, including Gojek, and asking them to take a chance on her despite having no traditional tech background. She describes her rapid career progression once she joined, building multiple teams from the ground up.
text_ko: Gojek 인사(HR)를 구글링해서 누군가에게 진짜 이메일을 보냈어요. "인도네시아로 이사할 의향이 있으니 저한테 한 번 기회를 주세요"라고 했고요. 그런데 진짜로 그렇게 해주셨고, 그래서 운이 엄청 좋았어요. 5년은 정말 순식간에 지나가요.
text_zh: 我当时就是谷歌搜了一下Gojek的HR邮箱，直接发邮件说："我愿意搬到印尼去，赌我一把吧。"结果他们真的答应了。我运气太好了。五年一眨眼就过去了。
text_es: Literalmente le mandé un email a alguien después de buscar en Google "HR Gojek" y le dije: "Estoy dispuesto a mudarme a Indonesia, dense una oportunidad conmigo." Y la verdad es que sí me la dieron. O sea, tuve una suerte increíble. Cinco años se pasan volando.
key_sentence: I got extremely lucky taking a bet on me.
original_text: I literally emailed someone after Googling HR at Gojek and said, 'I'm willing to move to Indonesia, take a bet on me.' And they actually did. So I got extremely lucky. Five years fly by insanely fast. I went through building out the data team from scratch.

vocabulary.definition: To make a decision or investment based on the belief that a person or idea will succeed, despite uncertainty.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, this phrase is often used when a company decides to invest in a startup or hire an individual based on potential rather than proven success.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase implies a level of risk-taking and optimism, and is often used in contexts where outcomes are unpredictable.

text: We would do things as simple as wanting to test a subscription feature, which was just released in Singapore a couple weeks ago. We ended up saying, 'We have this voucher system that we can distribute vouchers in the back end.
speaker: Crystal Widjaja
context: Lenny asks Crystal about scrappy growth tactics that Asian startups use which US companies could learn from. Crystal is explaining Gojek's approach of doing things that don't scale to validate ideas quickly. She's describing how they tested a subscription service concept without building any new technology - instead using existing systems like WhatsApp groups and manual backend processes to create a 'Wizard of Oz' experience that mimicked the final product.
text_ko: 저희는 몇 주 전에 싱가포르에서 막 출시된 구독 기능(subscription feature)을 테스트해보고 싶다 같은 단순한 일도 했어요. 결국 “백엔드(back end)에서 바우처를 배포할 수 있는 바우처 시스템(voucher system)이 있다”라고 말하게 됐죠.
text_zh: 我们做的事情其实很简单，就是想测试一下订阅功能，这个功能几周前刚在新加坡上线。结果我们就说，'我们有个优惠券系统，可以在后台发放优惠券。'
text_es: Hacíamos cosas tan sencillas como querer probar una función de suscripción que acababa de salir en Singapur hace un par de semanas. Al final dijimos: "Tenemos este sistema de cupones donde podemos distribuir cupones desde el back end."
key_sentence: We can distribute vouchers in the back end via WhatsApp.
original_text: We would do things as simple as wanting to test a subscription feature, which was just released in Singapore a couple weeks ago. We ended up saying, 'We have this voucher system that we can distribute vouchers in the back end. We obviously know our driver's phone numbers. Why don't we just add them to a WhatsApp group?'

vocabulary.definition: To spread or deliver something across a range of locations or to various recipients.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, distributing products, services, or information effectively is key to reaching target markets and maximizing sales.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply both physical distribution of goods and digital distribution of content or services, depending on the context.

vocabulary.definition: A service or functionality that requires users to pay a recurring fee to access or utilize it.
vocabulary.businessContext: Subscription features are commonly used in SaaS (Software as a Service) models, allowing companies to generate steady revenue while providing ongoing value to users.
vocabulary.nuance: The term suggests a commitment from users, which can enhance customer loyalty but may also require careful management of user expectations.

text: The only thing better than knowing... If you have data of what your customers are doing, that is the best data you could ever get.
speaker: Crystal Widjaja
context: Lenny asks whether Crystal advises startups to be more scrappy and do things that don't scale, given that US culture is different from Southeast Asia. Crystal responds by emphasizing the critical importance of getting real customer behavior data rather than just theorizing about what might work. She argues that any product idea that can't be tested experimentally isn't worth pursuing, regardless of how logical it might seem on paper.
text_ko: 아는 것보다 더 좋은 건, 고객이 실제로 무엇을 하고 있는지에 대한 데이터(data)를 갖고 있는 거예요. 그건 당신이 얻을 수 있는 최고의 데이터예요.
text_zh: 最好的数据就是了解你的客户在做什么，这比什么都管用。
text_es: Si tienes datos de lo que están haciendo tus clientes, esos son los mejores datos que puedes conseguir.
key_sentence: If you have data of what your customers are doing, that is the best data you could ever get.
original_text: The only thing better than knowing... If you have data of what your customers are doing, that is the best data you could ever get. And so if you don't have a tested hypothesis, if you can't think of a way to run an experiment, then honestly that idea is pretty useless.

vocabulary.definition: Facts, statistics, or information collected for analysis or reference.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, data is used to inform decision-making, track performance, and understand customer behavior.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'data' can imply raw numbers or information, but it is often used in conjunction with analytics to derive insights.

vocabulary.definition: Individuals or organizations that purchase goods or services from a business.
vocabulary.businessContext: Understanding customers is essential for businesses to tailor their offerings, enhance satisfaction, and drive loyalty.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'customers' can encompass various types of buyers, including end-users and clients, and implies a relationship based on exchange.

text: So mathematically speaking, you're going to get the same level of trends, but the precision at which you understand those trends will become more deep if you have more data.
speaker: Crystal Widjaja
context: Lenny asks how early-stage startups should approach experimentation when they have limited users and data. Crystal gives a counterintuitive response that you can and should run experiments even with very small sample sizes like 30 people. She explains the mathematical principle that while larger samples give you more precision, the fundamental trends and insights you discover will be similar regardless of whether you have 30 users or 300.
text_ko: 그러니까 수학적으로 보면(mathematically speaking), 추세(trends) 자체는 비슷하게 나타나요. 하지만 데이터가 많아질수록 그 추세를 이해하는 정밀도(precision)는 훨씬 높아져요.
text_zh: 从数学角度来说，趋势的大方向不会变，但是数据越多，你对这些趋势的理解就会越精准，越深入。
text_es: Hablando en términos matemáticos, vas a obtener el mismo nivel de tendencias, pero la precisión con la que entiendes esas tendencias va a ser mucho más profunda si tienes más datos.
key_sentence: Mathematically speaking, more data deepens understanding of trends.
original_text: So mathematically speaking, you're going to get the same level of trends, but the precision at which you understand those trends will become more deep if you have more data. But the underlying information that you're getting out of that won't be very different at larger scales.

vocabulary.definition: The quality of being exact, accurate, and clearly defined. Precision refers to the degree of refinement in measurement or expression.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, precision is crucial for data analysis, forecasting, and decision-making, as it impacts the reliability of insights derived from data.
vocabulary.nuance: While precision emphasizes accuracy, it can sometimes be confused with accuracy; precision is about consistency in measurements rather than their correctness.

vocabulary.definition: To grasp the meaning, significance, or nature of something. Understanding involves comprehending complex concepts or information.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, understanding is essential for effective communication, strategic planning, and problem-solving, as it allows stakeholders to make informed decisions.
vocabulary.nuance: Understanding can imply a deeper level of comprehension beyond mere knowledge, often involving the ability to apply insights in practical situations.

text: So to say, oh, this is the thing, instrumentation is what's wrong, I think it's a very actionable thing. It's probably one of the most solvable problems out there. It just takes some time and mental model shifts to do it well.
speaker: Crystal Widjaja
context: Lenny asks Crystal about her popular blog post 'Why Most Analytics Efforts Fail' and what the root causes are. Crystal explains that the main issue is instrumentation - how companies set up their data tracking. She's emphasizing that while many companies struggle with analytics, the problem is actually quite solvable once you understand that the issue isn't the tools or dashboards, but rather how you instrument and structure your data collection from the beginning.
text_ko: 그래서 '아, 이게 문제구나 — 계측(instrumentation)에 문제가 있네'라고 하는 건 제 생각에 꽤 실행 가능한 접근이에요. 아마 해결하기 쉬운 문제들 중 하나일 거예요. 다만 제대로 해내려면 시간과 사고 방식 전환(mental model shifts)이 좀 필요해요.
text_zh: 所以说，要找到问题的根源，仪表监控(instrumentation)才是关键，我觉得这个问题其实很好解决。这可能是最容易搞定的问题之一了，只是需要花点时间，转变一下思路就能做好。
text_es: O sea, decir "ah, este es el problema, la instrumentación es lo que está fallando", me parece algo muy accionable. Probablemente sea uno de los problemas más fáciles de resolver que hay. Solo requiere tiempo y cambiar un poco el chip mental para hacerlo bien.
key_sentence: Instrumentation is an actionable thing and one of the most solvable problems.

vocabulary.definition: Capable of being acted upon or implemented; providing clear guidance for action.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, actionable insights refer to data or information that can be directly applied to make decisions or drive strategies.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'actionable' implies feasibility, it is often used to emphasize the practicality of a suggestion or finding rather than its theoretical nature.

vocabulary.definition: Able to be resolved or dealt with; indicating that a problem has a solution.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business challenges, a solvable problem suggests that with the right resources and strategies, a resolution can be achieved, often fostering a proactive approach to problem-solving.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'solvable' carries a positive connotation, implying optimism about overcoming obstacles, but it may also downplay the complexity of certain issues.

vocabulary.definition: Changes in the underlying assumptions or frameworks through which individuals understand and interpret information.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and innovation, mental model shifts are crucial for adapting to new technologies or methodologies, enabling teams to embrace change and improve processes.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase suggests a deeper cognitive transformation, often requiring time and effort, and is typically used in discussions about organizational change or learning.

vocabulary.definition: The use of instruments or tools to measure, monitor, or control processes and systems.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, instrumentation refers to the implementation of metrics and analytics tools that provide insights into performance and user behavior, essential for data-driven decision-making.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'instrumentation' often relates to technical setups, it can also imply a strategic approach to understanding and optimizing business operations.

text: Do not treat metric gathering as entertainment. It's not there for you to be like, 'Oh, that's interesting, how novel,' and then not act on it. So real news is information that changes what you do in the real world.
speaker: Crystal Widjaja
context: Crystal is explaining why most analytics efforts fail by using an analogy about how people use Twitter. She compares looking at metrics just to see interesting patterns (without taking action) to using Twitter for entertainment rather than actual news. Crystal emphasizes that data should drive decision-making and behavior changes, not just provide interesting observations that teams discuss but never act upon.
text_ko: 지표 수집(metric gathering)을 오락거리로 다루지 마세요. '오, 흥미롭네, 신기하네' 하고 끝내고 아무 조치도 안 해서는 안 돼요. 진짜 뉴스는 실제로 당신의 행동을 바꾸게 하는 정보예요.
text_zh: 别把收集数据当成娱乐消遣。不是让你看了之后就"哇，挺有意思的，挺新鲜"，然后就没下文了。真正有价值的信息，是那种能让你在实际工作中改变做法的东西。
text_es: No trates la recolección de métricas como entretenimiento. No está ahí para que digas "Ay, qué interesante, qué curioso" y luego no hagas nada al respecto. Así que las noticias de verdad son información que cambia lo que haces en el mundo real.
key_sentence: Do not treat metric gathering as entertainment; real news changes your actions.

vocabulary.definition: The process of collecting and analyzing quantitative data to assess performance or progress towards specific goals.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, metric gathering is essential for evaluating the effectiveness of strategies, products, or services, enabling informed decision-making.
vocabulary.nuance: While often seen as a routine task, it should be approached with the intent to derive actionable insights rather than merely for data collection.

vocabulary.definition: To take action based on information or insights obtained from analysis or observation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, acting on data means implementing changes or strategies that are informed by metrics or analytics to drive improvement.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase implies a sense of urgency and responsibility, suggesting that one should not only understand the data but also respond to it effectively.

vocabulary.definition: The practical, everyday environment in which people live and work, as opposed to theoretical or abstract concepts.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, referring to the 'real world' emphasizes the importance of applying theories and strategies to tangible situations and outcomes.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase often carries a connotation of practicality and realism, suggesting that ideas must be tested and validated in actual circumstances.
